builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TID System for Speech-COSER Challenge 2026: ASR Track
summary: The method replaces full fine-tuning of an ASR model with a two-stage LoRA curriculum in which CTC pseudo-forced alignment scores filter or order training samples by audio-text match quality, followed by post-hoc magnitude pruning of the LoRA matrices. It costs little in memory since only low-rank adapters are trained, but adds pipeline complexity: alignment scoring, curriculum staging, pruning, and a seven-system ROVER ensemble for the best result. It can fail if alignment scores mislabel usable training data as mismatched, if pruning removes adapter capacity needed for the target domain, or if the ensemble inference cost is unacceptable in production.
rationale: LoRA fine-tuning is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU and the alignment-based data selection is cheap to replicate, but the WER benefit over standard LoRA fine-tuning is not isolated from the ensemble, so the reader must validate the individual components on their own speech data before adopting.
technique: Alignment-guided LoRA curriculum with pruning for ASR

claims.statement: The method replaces full fine-tuning of an ASR model with a two-stage LoRA curriculum in which CTC pseudo-forced alignment scores filter or order training samples by audio-text match quality, followed by post-hoc magnitude pruning of the LoRA matrices. It costs little in memory since only low-rank adapters are trained, but adds pipeline complexity: alignment scoring, curriculum staging, pruning, and a seven-system ROVER ensemble for the best result. It can fail if alignment scores mislabel usable training data as mismatched, if pruning removes adapter capacity needed for the target domain, or if the ensemble inference cost is unacceptable in production.
An ensemble of seven systems via ROVER achieves 36.25% unnormalized and 22.17% normalized WER on spontaneous elderly rural-Spanish speech.
